result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.rooted_product()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Compute the rooted product of this graph with a rooted graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.rooted_product()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Compute the rooted product of this graph with a rooted graph. title: >- [Graph.rooted_product()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Compute the rooted product of this graph with a rooted graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the rooted product of this graph with a rooted graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L39972-L40024){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.rooted_product( other, root, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Rooted product](/assets/graphs/rooted-product.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="G is a path 1–2–3–4 (accent edges) and H a tooth, an edge from top to tip (teal), rooted at top (outlined). The rooted product hangs a copy of the tooth from every node of G: the top row holds the roots (1, top) to (4, top), wired like G by accent edges, and each teal edge drops to that column's tip. The result is a comb with 8 nodes and 7 edges, a tree." width="100%"} The rooted product hangs a copy of `other` from every node of this graph: copy `g` consists of the nodes `(g, h)`, wired like `other`, and the copies are linked to each other only through their roots, `(g, root)`, which are wired like this graph. It builds structures such as combs (a path with a pendant path at every node), dendrimer-like molecules, and hierarchical networks where each site has the same local layout. Both graphs must be directed or both undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The rooted graph attached at every node. Neither graph is modified. [root]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The root node of `other` (ID or label). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with `n * m` nodes, numbered and labeled as in `cartesian_product()`; edges keep the weight and attributes of their factor edge. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graphs differ in directedness or `root` is not a node of `other`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The product has $|E_G| + n|E_H|$ edges, the subgraph induced by the roots is a copy of this graph, and every copy of `other` is attached at a single node, which is a cut node unless `other` is a single node. Matches NetworkX's `rooted_product`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A comb: a path of four teeth, each hanging a path of two nodes from its root: ::: {#d4879584 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec spine = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(4) tooth = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["top", "tip"]).add_edge("top", "tip") comb = spine.rooted_product(tooth, root="top") comb.count_nodes(), comb.count_edges(), comb.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (8, 7, True) ``` ::: :::
